newsitem.title: LEBANON: SOLIDERE end week mixed on market.
newsitem.headline: SOLIDERE end week mixed on market.

text.p: SOLIDERE shares were mixed on the Beirut Secondary Market (BSM) amid quiet trade in the week ended on Friday and dealers said few but considerable demand blocs were determining prices.
A shares rose to $105.25 on the privately-operated BSM from $104.625 last Friday and B shares dropped to $106.25 from $106.5.

"The market is still quiet. A few but relatively considerable blocs of demand orders are being placed on the trade margin -- between $104 and $106. There is nothing exceptional, no overdemand and no oversupply," a dealer told Reuters.
Weekly turnover on the BSM was 46,551 shares compared to 43,208 last week and value was $4,888,974 against $4,318,363.
On the official Beirut Stock Exchange, there was trade in only one of the four listed companies throughout the week.
Ciments Libanais closed at $1.2187 on Friday, up from $1.1875 last week. Total turnover on the BSE was 12,100 shares from 7,121 shares.
There was no trade throughout the week in the shares of the three other listed firms, Eternit, Ciments Blancs and and Uniceramic.
Market sources said during the week that SOLIDERE would move its shares from the BSM to the official stock exchange on September 30.
Officials at the BSE welcomed the move saying it would inject new blood into the market on which trade has been lacklustre since it reopened in January after a 13-year gap.
The capitalisation of the Beirut Stock Exchange is less than $400 million. SOLIDERE shares would add some $2 billion to the market.
The BLOM Stock Index (BSI) rose 0.58 percent during the week to 908.33 and the Lebanon Invest Share Price Index (LISPI) rose 0.42 percent to 81.92. Both indexes cover both markets.
